allObjections.title: Fallback chain thundering herd
allObjections.detail: CA-11-A.4 caps fallback at 3 hops but with 26 agents × avg 5 tools × parallel runs, a widespread outage of a primary tool like anthropic-api could trigger 100+ simultaneous fallback attempts to secondary tools, overwhelming them and cascading failures.

allObjections.title: Per-agent scoring data sparsity
allObjections.detail: CA-11-D.3 tracks scores per (agent, adapter, capability) triple, but many agent-tool combinations will see <10 invocations/month, making the 0.6×performance weight in Locked Rule 18 statistically meaningless and causing erratic tool selection behavior.

allObjections.title: CEO constraint explosion complexity
allObjections.detail: CA-11-E allows per-product per-agent constraints with both allowedTools and blockedTools arrays, creating 2^n possible constraint states that can silently conflict across products, making debugging tool selection failures a combinatorial nightmare.

allObjections.title: Per-Agent Scoring Creates Data Sparsity
allObjections.detail: CA-11-D.3's proposal to track performance scores per (agent, adapter, capability) triple will lead to extreme data sparsity. An agent may only invoke a specific tool for a niche capability a few times, making the resulting performance score statistically volatile and unreliable for ranking, potentially causing unstable and suboptimal tool selection.

allObjections.title: Fallback Chains Obscure True Invocation Cost
allObjections.detail: The fallback mechanism in CA-11-A.4, while capped at 3 hops, can lead to significant cost blowouts. If an agent's top-ranked tool is cheap but flaky, it may frequently fall back to a more expensive second- or third-choice tool, rapidly consuming the product's per-run budget (§7.6) on a single step without a clear per-invocation cost governor.

allObjections.title: ToolMenus Introduce Significant "Spec Debt"
allObjections.detail: CA-11-B introduces numerous new, unwired Orchestra adapters (Sentry, Datadog, Netlify, etc.) across the 26 ToolMenus. This creates significant 'spec debt' by canonizing aspirational tools, misrepresenting the system's current capabilities, and bloating the agent charters with placeholders that have no clear implementation path or capacity estimate, contrary to the already-deferred adapters in §8.1.

allObjections.title: Unclear Tool Selection Timing
allObjections.detail: CA-11-A.3 does not specify the exact timing of tool selection within the agent's lifecycle. It is unclear whether the tool is selected at the beginning of the step or dynamically during the execution. This ambiguity could lead to inconsistent behavior across different agents and steps.

allObjections.title: Potential Cost Overruns
allObjections.detail: The fallback mechanism in CA-11-A.4 could lead to significant cost overruns if the primary tool fails and the fallback tools are more expensive. There is no specified budget or cost control mechanism to prevent this.

allObjections.title: Lack of Detail on CEO Constraints
allObjections.detail: CA-11-E introduces CEO constraints but does not provide detailed scenarios or examples of how these constraints might be applied and resolved in practice. This lack of detail could lead to misunderstandings and misapplications of the constraints.

allObjections.title: Fallback chain fragility
allObjections.detail: CA-11-A.4 caps fallback at 3 hops without considering cumulative error propagation. In complex agents like #21 (Aggressive Crawl), consecutive retryable errors across tools could exhaust fallbacks mid-crawl, truncating critical interactions like modal probing or AI-agent validation. Unlike current OrchestratorHub's global error budget, per-agent chains lack cross-step resilience.

allObjections.title: Per-agent score sparsity
allObjections.detail: CA-11-D.3's per-agent performance scoring will suffer data sparsity for dormant/niche agents (e.g., #20 Environmental Impacts). With infrequent invocations, ranking formulas will rely on stale/bootstrap data, causing tool misselection. Current global Orchestra scoring aggregates all invocations, providing statistically robust rankings.

allObjections.title: Constraint-induced capability gaps
allObjections.detail: CA-11-E CEO constraints could create capability holes when allowedTools/blockedTools mismatch required contextTypes. If Agent #7 Design is blocked from v0/Lovable but Bolt.new lacks 'design' capability, the agent becomes non-functional. Current routing lacks such product-specific veto points.

allObjections.title: ToolMenu validator rigidity
allObjections.detail: CA-11-C.2's ≥3-tool minimum forces artificial entries for niche agents like #16 Productivity. This violates 'best-in-industry' principle by including subpar tools (e.g., PostHog for HR signals) solely to satisfy validator, degrading output quality versus today's capability-driven routing.

allObjections.title: Constraint layer can dead-end
allObjections.detail: CA-11-E.4 allows `allowedTools` and `blockedTools` to combine into an empty candidate set, and CA-11-A.3 then throws `RegistryError`. That means a stale ProductRegistry edit can hard-fail an agent before any fallback, even when the underlying global Orchestra still has viable adapters.

allObjections.title: Per-agent scores will starve
allObjections.detail: CA-11-D.3 introduces rolling outcome scores per `(agent, adapter, capability)` triple, but most agents only have a handful of invocations today. For dormant or low-frequency agents like #16 or #20, the ranking will be driven by sparse bootstraps and noisy first impressions, making the ToolMenu look precise while actually being underfit.

allObjections.title: Selection path increases nondeterminism
allObjections.detail: CA-11-A.4 combines per-invocation re-ranking, dynamic fallback, and mode-dependent user choice. Even with a 3-hop cap, the same agent/action can traverse different tools across retries due to latency and retryable errors, which weakens reproducibility relative to the current centralized OrchestratorHub routing.

allObjections.title: Insufficient fallback handling
allObjections.detail: CA-11-A.4's fallback chain is capped at min(toolMenu.length, 3), which may not be sufficient for agents with fewer than 3 tools. This could lead to premature exhaustion and failure.

allObjections.title: Lack of real-time adaptivity
allObjections.detail: CA-11-A.3's selectTool() method does not re-rank tools during fallback, potentially leading to suboptimal tool selection if the initial ranking is inaccurate or if runtime conditions change.

allObjections.title: Overly rigid ToolMenu structure
allObjections.detail: CA-11-B's flat ToolMenu for cross-step agents may not be suitable for all use cases, as different steps may require different tools. A stepKey-conditional ToolMenu could provide more flexibility.

allObjections.title: CA-11-A.4 fallback cap
allObjections.detail: The min(toolMenu.length, 3) cap in dispatchWithFallback still permits thundering-herd rate-limit cascades when three high-cost adapters (e.g. claude-code + openai-codex + devin) share the same upstream provider; no global back-pressure exists unlike the current OrchestratorHub.

allObjections.title: CA-11-B.10 TBD placeholders
allObjections.detail: Agents #22–#25 are listed with literal 'TBD' ToolMenus yet CA-11-C.2 validator will reject any roster entry having fewer than three concrete entries at promotion time, creating an immediate schema violation on first load.

allObjections.title: CA-11-D.3 score table bypass
allObjections.detail: The new flowai_agent_tool_outcome table writes per-(agent,adapter) scores without the prevHash / hash_chain_pointer discipline required by §14.2 GovernanceAuditLog, breaking the tamper-evidence invariant for all future tool-selection decisions.

perReviewer.overallNotes: My vote is conservative because CA-11 introduces a second ranking plane plus policy overlays that can fail in ways the current system does not. The most defensible next step is a limited spike, not full canonical promotion.

Q3.rationale: The added per-agent surfaces remove the single point of global visibility and audit that the current OrchestratorHub supplies.

Q4.rationale: Quarterly auto-updates would silently alter production behavior without the engagement filter required by Locked Rule 17.

Q5.rationale: Most agents will have far fewer than 30 invocations per (agent,adapter,capability) triple, rendering the new per-agent rank scores statistically unreliable.

Q6.pick_text: Reject — concept is unsound as specified
Q6.rationale: The design trades a single audited routing surface for 26 independent ones without demonstrated net reliability gains.
